meta.description: Single source of truth for the project's epistemic ontology. Defines spaces, tags, relation types, metadata fields, weight mappings, and the central working hypothesis referenced across nodes.json, nodes_freud.json, nodes_theory.json, edges.json, and edges_intra.json.
meta.note: All tags and relation types are declared exclusively here. Individual node files must adhere strictly to this schema.

space_A.name: Clinical Vignette (Primary Material)
space_A.description: Material under interpretation: lived events, symptoms, affects, personal interpretations, and objective environmental conditions from the synthetic clinical narrative.

space_B.name: Theoretical Corpus (Interpretive Lens)
space_B.description: Bounded conceptual and metapsychological frameworks used as the epistemic horizon to read Space A.

space_A.description: Passages concerning Walter's frailty, caregiving, death, and subsequent bereavement.
The symptom of compulsive self-talk/muttering: onset in domestic confinement, spillover into public streets, shame, and subsequent regulation through Argo.
Passages where Argo performs an explicit psychic or relational function for Clara: companionship, nocturnal alerting, co-regulation, presence at Walter's deathbed, and support in ongoing grief.
Anticipatory dread regarding the potential loss of Argo, combining symbolic bereavement anxiety and concrete rural hazards.
The ethical and psychic conflict between tethering Argo for safety and allowing him canine autonomy, including Clara's doubt over whose need the restriction truly serves.
Passages where Clara reflects on her own subjective state, affects, life trajectory, and the meaning she attributes to events rather than merely recounting facts.
Objective environmental hazards on the moor: poisoned baits, poultry feuds, adders, roaming intact dogs. Crucial for distinguishing realistic caution from neurotic projection.

space_B.description: Definitions and mechanisms of normal mourning: reality-testing, piecemeal withdrawal of libido (decathexis), work of mourning, continuing bonds, and symbolic rituals.
Clinical and metapsychological features of melancholia: impoverishment of the ego, unconscious aspect of the loss, self-reproach, and narcissistic identification.
Object-relations and metapsychological object theory: lost love-object, libidinal cathexis, living transitional object (Winnicott), selfobject (Kohut), and Lacanian object-lack.
Signal anxiety before threatened loss, anticipatory grief, and the Lacanian tear or hole in the Real.
space_B.note: Absent in Freud's 1917 essay; introduced exclusively via the complementary theoretical synthesis.

space_B.description: Coexistence of love and hate toward the same object: precondition for melancholia in Freud, and irreducible even in human-animal attachment according to Marie Bonaparte.
Introjection of the abandoned object into the ego ('the shadow of the object fell upon the ego'); core mechanism of Freudian melancholia.
space_B.note: Exclusive to the classical Freudian framework in this corpus.

space_B.description: Specificity of the human-animal bond: anthrozoology, psychic economy of companion animals, somatic co-regulation, and multispecies kinship.
space_B.note: Specific to the complementary theoretical corpus.

space_B.description: Socially unacknowledged bereavement (Doka): dissonance between internal devastation and external demands for normalcy, producing shame, isolation, and blocked mourning.
Clinical and therapeutic approaches to bereavement and companion-animal loss: validation, guilt deconstruction, narrative reconstruction, and memorial rituals.
space_B.note: Minimal usage in v0.2; serves as optional clinical orientation rather than a primary diagnostic node.

unused_tags.reason: Reserved for future iterations in which the researcher's own interpretive hypotheses are instantiated as first-class graph nodes.

relation_types.description: Directed edge types used across edges.json and edges_intra.json. Each relation carries a distinct epistemic function governing retrieval and LLM synthesis.

types.description: A clinical node exemplifies or embodies a theoretical concept (or parallels an earlier clinical pattern). Instantiation relation.
A theoretical concept serves directly as an interpretive tool explaining the clinical passage.
A node stands in tension with, refutes, or resists another clinical statement or theoretical claim. Adversative relation.
A node introduces an exception, boundary condition, or added complexity to a theoretical or narrative claim.
A clinical passage raises an interpretive question that the theoretical node leaves unresolved or answers only partially.
types.special_handling: Hermeneutic rather than assertive relation. During generation, the LLM must articulate and sustain the open tension as a genuine inquiry rather than forcing diagnostic closure.

types.description: Causal, temporal, or logical-argumentative progression strictly within the same space (clinical-to-clinical in Space A, or concept-to-concept in Space B).

metadata_fields.description: Schema for node metadata, specifying which fields are embedded into dense vectors versus reserved for structured graph traversal.

fields.description: Primary textual passage of the node.
Controlled ontology labels used for filtering and structural analysis.

Epistemic status of the chunk: event_account, observation, memory, personal_interpretation, open_question, definition, theoretical_claim, mechanism_description, conceptual_distinction, clinical_description, theoretical_conclusion, synthesis, theoretical_revision, clinical_proposal, historical_reference.
Rhetorical/logical role in Space B: define, contextualize, explain, describe, contrast, distinguish, argue, synthesize, propose, expand, question, legitimize, establish_condition, illustrate.

Researcher's analytical reading of the node: why it matters, what tensions it opens, and how it relates to the working hypothesis. Intentionally concatenated during embedding to steer semantic retrieval toward argumentatively salient passages.
fields.epistemic_warning: Vectorizing researcher notes deliberately biases retrieval toward a situated reading; it is a hermeneutic choice, not a neutral index.

intra_space_edges.description: Intra-space edges within Space A (narrative causality and internal tensions) and Space B (conceptual derivations and inter-theoretical debates). Implemented in edges_intra.json to enable multi-hop reasoning.

central_hypothesis.statement: The clinical material is more rigorously understood as an ongoing mourning process in which Argo performs an affective and symbolic mediating function, rather than as sufficient evidence of a melancholic organization in the strict Freudian sense.
central_hypothesis.instruction: Treat this statement as a working hypothesis to be tested against the graph: gather supporting evidence, surface complicating passages, and weigh rival theoretical readings without forcing premature diagnostic closure.
